How streaming translation works on a long article

This page exists to exercise the extension: it carries prose, links, code, hidden menus and content that appears later.

Reference paragraphs

Content scripts run inside an isolated world and therefore cannot touch the page's JavaScript variables directly, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 1.

The service worker suspends itself after a short idle period, so every request must be resumable after a restart, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 2.

IntersectionObserver reports visibility changes without forcing a layout pass on every scroll event, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 3.

Token budgets decide how many paragraphs a single request can carry before the gateway starts rejecting traffic, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 4.

Caching turns a repeat visit into an instant render because the same sentence never needs a second round trip, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 5.

Streaming responses let the reader watch sentences arrive instead of waiting for the whole article to finish, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 6.

Batch assembly groups neighbouring paragraphs so the model keeps terminology consistent across a section, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 7.

Restoring the original must be lossless, which means the untouched text is kept in memory for every written node, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 8.

Mutation observers catch infinite scroll feeds and single page navigation without a full rescan of the document, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 9.

Rate limiting is reported by response headers, and the extension waits for the reset window before retrying, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 10.

Scroll prefetching starts the next two screens early so the reader rarely notices a placeholder, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 11.

Whitespace handling keeps the leading and trailing spaces around inline links so the sentence still reads correctly, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 12.

Error reporting shows the raw gateway message instead of a friendly lie when a request is rejected, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 13.

Selection of units skips code blocks, form inputs and hidden menus because those strings are not prose, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 14.

Concurrency stays low enough to avoid throttling while keeping two requests in flight for smoother output, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 15.

Progress reporting counts finished paragraphs from the queue rather than estimating a percentage, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 16.

Dynamic pages inject fresh paragraphs long after load, and those paragraphs must join the same queue, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 17.

Long articles are translated from the reader's viewpoint outward, not from the top of the document, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 18.

Interface labels inside buttons and navigation bars are translated as ordinary text segments, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 19.

Language detection keeps numeric tables and URL strings untouched because translating them adds noise, which is why the extension keeps a queue keyed by document order and promotes whatever the reader is about to look at. See the reference page for the full list of edge cases, or read the migration notes before shipping anything to production. Paragraph number 20.

Code must stay untouched

const client = new Groq();
completion.on("chunk", (c) => process.stdout.write(c.choices[0].delta.content || ""));
Secret menu item that should never be translated.
Brand asset text with translate no attribute.
